questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.stem: Series 1 - 1 + 1 - 1 + ... has r = -1. Converge?

options.text: Yes, alternating terms cancel.
Yes, |r| = 1 is allowed.
No, partial sums oscillate 1,0.
No, because terms do not tend to zero? they do not? actually terms are ±1

questions.explanation: With |r| = 1, the geometric series does not converge; partial sums oscillate. Terms do not tend to zero either.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.stem: Planner Aria notes a finite geometric sum always exists, but infinite?

options.text: Infinite always converges to a/(1-r).
Infinite never converges.
Infinite converges only if r positive.
Infinite converges only if |r| < 1.

questions.explanation: A finite geometric sum always exists, but an infinite one converges only when |r| < 1. Positivity is not required.
